finding.summary: Redirect-guard tests cannot detect removal of `redirect: 'manual'` — the stub fetch ignores the init argument entirely
finding.evidence: The whole per-hop SSRF guard in `createImageFetcher` (packages/cli/src/docs/image-fetcher.ts:221) depends on passing `{ redirect: 'manual' }` so the loop, not `fetch`, owns the hop. Every test in `describe('createImageFetcher')` (lines 186-341) uses a stub `typeof globalThis.fetch` that only reads `input` and unconditionally returns a synthetic 301/302 `Response`; none of them assert anything about the second argument. If `redirect: 'manual'` were dropped, the stub would still hand back the 302, the loop would still re-check the Location, and 're-checks the target of a redirect instead of following it blindly' would still pass — while real `fetch` would silently auto-follow to `http://169.254.169.254/...` with no check in between. Nothing in the suite pins the option (grep for `redirect` in packages/cli/test returns no assertion).

verdict.reason: The finding claims no test in the suite pins `redirect: 'manual'` on the fetch call. A dedicated test exists: packages/cli/test/image-fetcher.test.ts:362-387, 'asks fetch not to follow redirects, on every hop'. Its stub fetch signature is `async (_input, init)` and it pushes `init?.redirect` into a `modes` array, returning a 302 on the first call and a 200 on the second, then asserts `expect(modes).toEqual(['manual', 'manual'])` (line 386). If `redirect: 'manual'` were removed from `fetchImpl(current, { redirect: 'manual' })` at packages/cli/src/docs/image-fetcher.ts:319, `modes` would be `[undefined, undefined]` and the test would fail — precisely the mutation the reviewer says is undetectable. The finding's quoted evidence is also wrong about the file: the `describe('createImageFetcher')` block spans lines 196-548, not 186-341, so the reviewer's read appears to have stopped before the option-pinning test; and a `redirect` assertion does exist in packages/cli/test, contrary to the claimed empty grep.
